question.text: During a routine portfolio review, it emerges that Agni Cat II AIF's Manager is considering a co-investment in an investee company where the Manager's CIO personally holds 4% equity via a family trust. As the AIF Compliance Officer escalating to the Trustee, the CORRECT treatment under the SEBI (AIF) Conflict-of-Interest framework is:

answer.text: No action required — co-investment by the CIO is a personal matter.
The CIO must exit his personal holding within 30 days automatically.
The Manager must issue a redemption notice to all LPs.

Disclose the conflict to existing and prospective investors BEFORE any allocation, route through the documented Conflict-of-Interest policy, and obtain appropriate governance clearance (e.g., LPAC / Trustee) before execution.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 7 lists — 'Conflicts, within Co-Investments by the Manager, shall be disclosed to the potential investors and existing investors, BEFORE any allocation being made towards these investments.' Every AIF must maintain a Conflict-of-Interest policy to identify and mitigate such potential conflicts; disclosure + governance escalation is mandatory, not automatic divestment. The Trap: Option A ignores the fiduciary duty. Option B invents a 30-day forced sell. Option C confuses conflict-handling with redemption mechanics — an irrelevant procedural lever. Cross-Exam Context: X-A/X-B (Investment Adviser) tests personal-trading conflict-disclosure from an RIA angle; XXIV (AML) tests insider-related reporting; XIX-C integrates the AIF-specific manager conflict policy. Manager's Pro-Tip: Build a 'deal-specific conflict matrix' that the IC ticks off for every investment memo. An LPAC sign-off trail is your best defence if SEBI inspects years later.
